{{Short description|Japanese molecular geneticist}}
'''Jun'ichi Tomizawa''' (Japanese: 富澤 純一 Tomizawa Jun'ichi; June 24, 1924 – January 26, 2017, in [[Mishima, Shizuoka]], Japan) was a Japanese [[Molecular genetics|molecular geneticist]].

== Life and work ==
Tomizawa completed his [[pharmacology]] studies at the [[University of Tokyo]] in 1947 under the guidance of Morizo Ishidate. Following that, he worked at the Japanese National Institute of Health, conducting research on DNA replication in bacteriophages. From 1957, he collaborated with [[Alfred Hershey|Alfred Day Hershey]] at the [[Carnegie Institution for Science|Carnegie Institution of Washington]] and later with Cyrus Levinthal at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]. Returning to the Japanese National Institute of Health in 1960, he assumed leadership of the Chemistry Department in 1961 and conducted courses on [[bacteriophage]] biology at [[Kanazawa University]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Ogawa |first1=Hideyuki |last2=Ogawa |first2=Tomoko |date=2018-07-13 |title=In memory of Jun-ichi Tomizawa, Professor Emeritus of the National Institute of Genetics |journal=Genes to Cells |language=en |volume=23 |issue=7 |pages=508–511 |doi=10.1111/gtc.12595 |pmid=30003646 |issn=1356-9597|doi-access=free }}</ref>

In 1965, Tomizawa was appointed as a professor and head of the Biology Department at [[Osaka University]]. He later moved to the United States in 1971 to work at the [[National Institutes of Health]]. From 1989 until his retirement in 1997, Tomizawa served as the Director of the [[National Institute of Genetics]] in [[Mishima, Shizuoka|Mishima]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Outline & History::National Institute of Genetics |url=https://www.nig.ac.jp/nig/about-nig/outline-history |access-date=2023-12-15 |website=www.nig.ac.jp}}</ref> Additionally, from 1996 to 2006, he served as the founding editor of the scientific journal ''Genes to Cells'', the official publication of the Japanese Society for Molecular Biology.

Tomizawa was recognized as a pioneer in molecular biology in Japan.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-02-02 |title=富沢純一さん死去 日本の分子生物学の草分け：朝日新聞デジタル |trans-title=Junichi Tomizawa, Pioneer of Molecular Biology in Japan, Dies |url=https://www.asahi.com/articles/ASK1Y5SNCK1YULBJ008.html |access-date=2023-12-15 |website=asahi.com |archive-date=2017-02-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202054626/https://www.asahi.com/articles/ASK1Y5SNCK1YULBJ008.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> He significantly contributed to understanding the mechanisms of gene replication, notably discovering replication control through [[RNA]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=朝日賞 1971－2000年度 {{!}} 朝日新聞社の会社案内 |trans-title=Asahi Rewards 1971–2000 |url=https://www.asahi.com/corporate/award/asahi/12738070 |access-date=2023-12-15 |website=asahi.com |language=ja}}</ref> According to the [[Scopus]] database (as of October 2019), Tomizawa had an [[h-index]] of 43.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Scopus preview – Tomízawa, Junichi – Author details – Scopus |url=https://www.scopus.com/authid/detail.uri?authorId=16533189200 |access-date=2023-12-15 |website=www.scopus.com}}</ref> He actively supported and mentored numerous [[Doctorate|doctoral]] and [[Habilitation|postdoctoral]] students. Moreover, he donated 150 million [[Japanese yen|yen]] from his private funds to establish a program benefiting young scientists in life sciences.

For his contributions, Tomizawa received several honors: he was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1971,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Members of the American Academy of Arts & Sciences: 1780–2017 |url=https://www.amacad.org/sites/default/files/academy/multimedia/pdfs/publications/bookofmembers/ChapterT.pdf |access-date=2023-12-15 |website=amacad.org}}</ref> the [[Japan Academy|Japan Academy of Sciences]] in 1990,<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=物故会員個人情報 – 富澤純一｜日本学士院 |trans-title=Member Profile {{!}} The Japan Academy |url=https://www.japan-acad.go.jp/japanese/members/bukko/t_gyo/tomizawa_junichi.html |access-date=2023-12-15 |website=www.japan-acad.go.jp}}</ref> and the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 1995.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Jun-ichi Tomizawa |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/jun-ichi-tomizawa-haoypq/ |access-date=2023-12-15 |website=www.nasonline.org}}</ref> He was awarded the [[Asahi Prize]] in 1986<ref name=":0" /> and was named a [[Person of Cultural Merit]] in 2000.<ref name=":1" />
